meta.title: A Lightweight and Explainable NIDS for Cross-Dataset Generalization and False-Positive Reduction
meta.data_notice: SIMULATED DATA. The numbers in this report come from schema-faithful synthetic stand-ins for UNSW-NB15 and CIC-IDS2017, not from the real datasets. They demonstrate the pipeline and the measurement methodology, not real-world performance.

schema.note: Bucketed to avoid memorising dataset-specific port numbers. UNSW has hex-valued ports (dropped).
Unit conversion; flow-termination rules differ between exporters (Argus vs CICFlowMeter).
CIC reports payload only; header bytes are re-added with an assumed 40 B/packet. Residual mismatch remains.
Directional counts. Direction definitions follow each exporter.
Computed from aligned fields, NOT from native smean/dmean or Average Packet Size.
Native CIC Flow Bytes/s contains inf/NaN, so it is recomputed identically for both datasets.
No CIC equivalent; also a known shortcut feature in UNSW (attack traffic generator leaves TTL fingerprints).
Argus connection states and CIC TCP flag counts are not equivalent.
Similar-sounding names, different definitions (source-only ms vs bidirectional us). Not assumed equal.
Used ONLY to build leakage-aware groups for splitting; never given to a model.

findings.title: UNSW→CIC: macro-F1 falls from 0.91 to 0.47
findings.text: Same-dataset macro-F1 is 0.914 ± 0.004 but the unseen dataset gives 0.470 ± 0.005. Benign false-alarm rate moves from 1.30 ± 0.10 % to 1.12 ± 0.09 % (130 → 112 alerts per 10,000 benign flows) while the attack detection rate is 37.0 ± 0.7 %. Classes that collapse (recall < 0.2): DoS, Exploit, Botnet. Classes that transfer well (recall ≥ 0.8): Recon.

findings.title: CIC→UNSW: macro-F1 falls from 0.88 to 0.38
findings.text: Same-dataset macro-F1 is 0.879 ± 0.003 but the unseen dataset gives 0.377 ± 0.008. Benign false-alarm rate moves from 1.36 ± 0.07 % to 1.68 ± 0.12 % (136 → 168 alerts per 10,000 benign flows) while the attack detection rate is 18.6 ± 1.0 %. Classes that collapse (recall < 0.2): DoS, Recon, Botnet. No class transfers with recall ≥ 0.8.

findings.title: Transfer is asymmetric
findings.text: Macro-F1 drop is 0.445 ± 0.004 for UNSW→CIC and 0.503 ± 0.010 for CIC→UNSW; the two target scores differ by 0.093 ± 0.007. Which dataset is used as source matters, as reported by Layeghy & Portmann (2022).

findings.title: UNSW→CIC: alerts per 10k benign — default 112, global 213, per-class 208, FPR-cap 36
findings.text: On the unseen dataset, per-class cost thresholds give about the same benign alert volume as a single global threshold (208 vs 213 per 10,000 benign flows), with macro-F1 0.543 vs 0.543. Against the default arg-max rule (0.470, 112 alerts) they raise macro-F1 but produce more false alerts, because the cost matrix charges a missed attack more than a false alarm. The FPR-cap policy is the false-positive-reduction setting: 36 alerts per 10,000 benign flows at macro-F1 0.333. All thresholds were learned on source validation data only.

findings.title: CIC→UNSW: alerts per 10k benign — default 168, global 622, per-class 691, FPR-cap 47
findings.text: On the unseen dataset, per-class cost thresholds give higher benign alert volume than a single global threshold (691 vs 622 per 10,000 benign flows), with macro-F1 0.553 vs 0.545. Against the default arg-max rule (0.377, 168 alerts) they raise macro-F1 but produce more false alerts, because the cost matrix charges a missed attack more than a false alarm. The FPR-cap policy is the false-positive-reduction setting: 47 alerts per 10,000 benign flows at macro-F1 0.293. All thresholds were learned on source validation data only.

findings.title: Source-fitted calibration under shift
findings.text: Top-label ECE on the unseen dataset: UNSW→CIC 0.084 → 0.082 after isotonic calibration; CIC→UNSW 0.098 → 0.084. Calibration is fitted on source validation data, so a change here measures how well it survives the shift.

findings.title: UNSW→CIC: top-5 SHAP overlap 4.2 / 5
findings.text: Top-5 feature overlap between source and target is 4.2 ± 0.4 of 5; Spearman rank correlation of importance is 0.86 ± 0.04. Across features, rank shift correlates with benign distribution shift (KS) at ρ = 0.49 ± 0.19 and with attribution enrichment on errors at ρ = 0.13 ± 0.21 (up to 300 errors probed per seed; 13 features, so treat these as indicative).

findings.title: CIC→UNSW: top-5 SHAP overlap 3.8 / 5
findings.text: Top-5 feature overlap between source and target is 3.8 ± 0.4 of 5; Spearman rank correlation of importance is 0.56 ± 0.09. Across features, rank shift correlates with benign distribution shift (KS) at ρ = -0.19 ± 0.16 and with attribution enrichment on errors at ρ = 0.40 ± 0.21 (up to 300 errors probed per seed; 13 features, so treat these as indicative).

findings.title: UNSW→CIC replay: p50 2.96 ms/flow, 821562 pkts/s
findings.text: 4000 flows / 71637 packets replayed. Single-flow latency (feature build + preprocessing + model + calibration + decision): p50 2.96 ms, p95 3.88 ms, p99 4.52 ms. Flow export 2227962 pkts/s; micro-batched scoring 72671 flows/s; end-to-end 821562 pkts/s. Alert volume: 354 alerts, 215 per 10,000 benign flows. Exporter feature round-trip max relative error: 3.50e-12. Measured on 12 CPUs; re-measure on your own machine for the report.

findings.title: CIC→UNSW replay: p50 2.62 ms/flow, 864893 pkts/s
findings.text: 4000 flows / 70812 packets replayed. Single-flow latency (feature build + preprocessing + model + calibration + decision): p50 2.62 ms, p95 3.66 ms, p99 3.86 ms. Flow export 2254556 pkts/s; micro-batched scoring 79262 flows/s; end-to-end 864893 pkts/s. Alert volume: 464 alerts, 622 per 10,000 benign flows. Exporter feature round-trip max relative error: 1.10e-12. Measured on 12 CPUs; re-measure on your own machine for the report.

limitations: All numbers come from SIMULATED stand-ins for UNSW-NB15 and CIC-IDS2017. They validate the pipeline and measurement method, not real-world detection performance. Re-run on the real CSVs before reporting any result.

The distribution shift between the two datasets was designed into the generator (signature shifts per attack class). Which classes collapse and by how much is therefore a property of the simulation, not a finding about the real datasets.

The gradient-boosted model is scikit-learn's HistGradientBoosting (XGBoost was not installable here); the MLP is scikit-learn's MLPClassifier (PyTorch was not installable). The XGBoost/PyTorch code paths are included but were not executed here.
SHAP values are computed with a permutation-sampling Shapley estimator (the quantity SHAP approximates), not the `shap` package. With the package installed, exact TreeSHAP can be used for XGBoost.

Replay uses packets synthesised from held-out flows and a minimal Python flow exporter, not real PCAPs or CICFlowMeter. Latency/throughput are real wall-clock measurements on the sandbox machine (CPU count in the environment block) and will differ on your laptop.

Only flow features shared by both datasets are used (13). Port number is bucketed, TTL, TCP state/flags and inter-arrival features are excluded because they are not comparable across the two exporters.
Five seeds vary splits and model initialisation; the two datasets themselves are fixed, so the reported standard deviation does not include dataset-sampling variability.
Class mapping merges CIC web attacks into 'Exploit' and UNSW 'Backdoor' into 'Botnet'. These are approximations and should be reviewed against the real data.
